title: How do I pay a borrower's past-due Auto Loans installment from their PCB checking account?
content:
# How do I pay a borrower's past-due Auto Loans installment from their PCB checking account?

This entry of the Auto Loans product category at PCB applies when a borrower asks PCB to pay the earliest past-due installment of an auto loan by a transfer from the borrower's own PCB checking account. It is handled on the borrower's request.

## Policy

1. The agent posts **one** scheduled payment, credited toward that installment.
2. The payment does not advance past the installment it satisfies, and it never satisfies a later installment early.

Observable effect for the borrower: the payment, its split between fees, interest and principal, and the updated balances appear on the loan once it posts.

## Tool: post_installment_payment_660c6229

**Situation of use and capability.** Posts one scheduled auto loan payment that the borrower pays by transfer from their own PCB checking account, credited today toward one installment of the loan. One call books the payment on the loan's activity as a scheduled payment made by PCB transfer, with the total split into the fees, interest and principal parts given; when the fees part is above zero it also books the matching fee settlement entry. On the loan it lowers the unpaid principal by the principal part and the unpaid fees by the fees part, records today as the last payment date, and records the next installment due date and the days past due given.

**How it is invoked.** An internal tool of the agent: it must first be unlocked with unlock_agent_discoverable_tool and then called with call_agent_discoverable_tool.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| auto_loan_id | the auto loan reference number of the loan being paid, from the auto loan lookup for this borrower | reference number |
| installment_due_date | the due date of the installment this payment is credited toward; never empty for this payment | YYYY-MM-DD |
| amount | the total payment drawn from the checking account | USD, positive, 2 decimal places |
| fees_portion | the part of the payment applied to fees due | USD, 2 decimal places, 0.00 when no fees are paid |
| interest_portion | the part of the payment applied to accrued interest | USD, 2 decimal places |
| principal_portion | the part of the payment applied to principal | USD, 2 decimal places |
| counterparty_account_id | the checking account reference number of the borrower's PCB checking account the money is drawn from, from the checking account lookup | reference number |
| next_payment_due_date | the due date of the earliest installment that will still be unsatisfied once this payment posts | YYYY-MM-DD |
| days_past_due | the loan's days past due once this payment posts | non-negative whole number of calendar days, 0 when no installment is past due |

**Return.** On success the receipt shows status "posted" with: payment_reference (the 12-digit payment reference number), auto_txn_id (reference number of the new payment entry), fee_settlement_id (reference number of the fee settlement entry, or empty when the fees part is 0.00), principal_balance and fees_due afterwards (USD, 2 decimal places), next_payment_due_date (YYYY-MM-DD) and days_past_due (whole number).

## Basis Q&A

**Can one call pay two missed installments?** No. One call posts one scheduled payment credited toward one installment, and a payment never satisfies a later installment early.

**What shows that the call worked?** A receipt with status "posted" and a payment reference number.
